svg.text: Facebook / Meta — Feature → Data Model → Store
User Profiles
Model: Document — profile is a self-contained tree (name, bio, photos[], work[], education[])
Store: TAO (MySQL shards + graph cache) for entity; profile blob likely in a key-value store
Trade-off: 1-to-many (work history) embeds naturally. But profile → friends = many-to-many → needs graph layer (TAO edges).
LinkedIn equiv: Espresso (document, Avro, sub-keys for 1-to-many)
Friends List / Social Graph
Model: Graph — vertices (users) + edges (friendships). Many-to-many is THE data.
Store: TAO — graph cache over MySQL shards. Objects (vertices) + Associations (edges) + Assoc counts.
Trade-off: TAO is simpler than Neo4j — no multi-hop queries. For friend-of-friend, Meta pre-computes and caches.
LinkedIn equiv: Liquid (in-memory graph, Prologin, supports real-time multi-hop traversals unlike TAO)
Likes / Reactions
Model: Graph edge — (user)--[LIKES]-->(post). Many-to-many: many users like many posts.
Store: TAO association + counter cache. The "3.2K likes" count is pre-aggregated (not computed on read).
Trade-off: Storing each like as a row = write-heavy (millions/sec). Counter cache = eventual consistency (you might see 3.2K
for a few seconds before it updates to 3.3K). Worth it: reads >> writes for counts.
LinkedIn equiv: Espresso (junction table) + Pinot (real-time like counts aggregation)
Comments (Threaded)
Model: Document (tree) — 1-to-many: post → comments. But replies create nesting → tree within tree.
Store: TAO for the comment entity + association (post → comments). Threaded: adjacency list or closure table.
Trade-off: Adjacency list (parentId) = easy writes, hard deep reads. Closure table = fast reads, expensive writes.
Recommendation mention creates many-to-many: comment → mentioned user. Mentions need graph edges.
LinkedIn equiv: Espresso (sub-keys: _key=postId, _subKey1=commentId) + Galene (search comments)
Messages / Chat (Messenger, WhatsApp)
Model: Document (time-series) — 1-to-many: conversation → messages, ordered by timestamp.
Store: HBase / MyRocks for message storage (append-heavy, time-ordered). Memcache for recent.
Trade-off: LSM-tree (HBase/MyRocks) is write-optimized (fast appends). But range scans for "load older messages"
need sorted storage. B-tree (MySQL) would be slower for writes but faster for random reads.
LinkedIn equiv: Espresso (_key=memberId, _subKey1=convId). WhatsApp: custom Erlang + Mnesia.
News Feed / Timeline
Model: Materialized view (pre-computed) — fan-out on write: when user posts, push to followers' feed caches.
Store: TAO (feed edges) + Memcache (rendered feed) + ML ranking service (scores per item).
Trade-off: Fan-out on write = fast reads (timeline pre-built) but celebrity problem (100M followers = 100M writes).
Meta uses hybrid like Twitter: fan-out for normal users, pull-on-read for celebrities. Ranking applied at read time.
LinkedIn equiv: Espresso (feed store) + Venice (pre-computed feed ranking scores) + Kafka (fan-out events)
Followers / Subscribers
Model: Graph edge (directed)
(A)--[FOLLOWS]-->(B)
Asymmetric: A follows B
≠ B follows A
Store: TAO assoc + count
Video Metadata (YouTube/Reels)
Model: Document (self-contained)
{title, desc, tags[], thumbnails[],
duration, uploaderId, viewCount}
Store: Vitess (MySQL shards)
+ Bigtable (view counts)
